dedupe_keys.name: evaluating traffic control strategies for autonomous shuttle in different av penetration using sumo traffic simulation

description: The documented SUMO application compares mixed-traffic, dynamic-lane and separated-lane strategies on a Turin road section over five autonomous-vehicle penetration levels. Simulation results distinguish shuttle travel-time benefits from adverse effects on other vehicles; the dynamic lane offers a smaller disruption tradeoff than the separated lane in the studied conditions. These are scenario outcomes, not observed improvements from a completed city-wide deployment. The source authors provide the native description and file descriptors through Zenodo. Only metadata was inspected; no measurements, archives, source code or document bodies were retrieved. Public access and the deposit document licence do not establish executable access, software reuse rights or operating costs. Coverage remains bounded to the named experiments, with other geographic and temporal fields unknown. Related project resources may overlap; common project membership does not establish identical simulation inputs or results.
name: Evaluating Traffic Control Strategies for Autonomous Shuttle in Different AV Penetration, Using SUMO Traffic Simulation
